derivation: min_door_width_m IS A DESIGN MINIMUM, NOT THE BAKE'S. The bake needs the doorway erosion leaves: min_door_width >= 2*ceil(agent_radius/cell_size)*cell_size + 2*cell_size, which at this contract's nav_bake (radius 0.4, cell 0.1) is 2*4*0.1 + 0.2 = 1.00. It was first worked at a 0.15 m cell -- 2*ceil(0.4/0.15)*0.15 + 0.3 = 1.2, ratified 1.25 for margin -- and when cell_size_m moved to 0.1 (nav_bake.cell_size_derivation) the 1.25 stayed. The walker kept it, 2026-10-13, as the width a walkable door is built to: a 0.35 m body passes it with 0.275 m a side. Deli Counter writes every walkable door it makes at it -- presets.DOOR_W, a width-less door's default (spec_types.Opening.resolved), the staff door behind a teller line (level_design._STAFF_DOOR_WIDTH) -- and builds the island aisle (level_design.island_aisle_width) and the stair landing's opening (stairwell, 0.8 + this) from it, so lowering it toward 1.00 narrows every one of them. What was widened to meet it, and the two doors that are not: min_door_width_note. min_corridor = 2*agent_radius + 0.3 body margin.
min_door_width_note: THE DOORS WERE WIDENED TO THIS NUMBER; THE NUMBER WAS NOT LOWERED TO THE DOORS (Deli Counter 0.214.0, factory roadmap 197). The walker, 2026-10-13: 'If we change the door widths, that's ok, it should be called out in the agent contract' -- and, asked which way, 'widen the doors and keep 1.25'. Before 0.214.0 the library built 200 walkable doors under 1.25 in 32 of 132 enterable buildings -- 13 at 1.0 m, 74 at 1.1, 113 at 1.2, 47 of those width-less and so at the builder's own default, then 1.2 -- and the presets wrote 61 more at 1.1 and 1.2. None was under the bake's 1.00 (see derivation), and the library's shells all passed the nav gate. Since 0.214.0 a width-less door resolves to this, every preset writes its doors at it, the staff door asks for it, and migrate_door_width.py widened the library's 152 authored doors about their own centres, one slid along its wall clear of a partition's end (final_stand's west_entry). TWO DOORS STAY UNDER IT, named so they are not read as oversights. primos_pizza's kitchen_stairs stays 1.20 m: between a partition's end (layout_lint L18) and the basement stair's hole (L21) no place on that wall holds 1.25, so it widens when the stair moves (migrate_door_width.KEPT). The landing doors stairs-first generation punches are the corridor's width, min_corridor_width_m, 1.1 m today (stair_core._PUNCH_DOOR_W): every crossing one is punched in measured 1.1 to 1.2 m, so at 1.25 none of the 20 in stair_regression's 140 variants is punched and its checks fail 21 times against 2; Level Factory never builds stairs-first. An Empty's doors are shut and nothing walks through them, so they keep theirs. Held by test_door_width.py; validate.py's navigability check only warns on a door under this.
re_derive_when: characters.player.radius_m moves -- and with it nav_bake.agent_radius_m, the fattest body plus 0.05 -- or nav_bake.cell_size_m moves. Re-derive min_corridor_width_m (2*agent_radius + 0.3) and the bake's door floor in derivation. min_door_width_m must stay at or over that floor, and test_door_width.py fails until the derivation's figure and the floor agree; it is a design number, so choose what it becomes rather than letting it fall to the floor -- it gives a body (min_door_width - 2*radius)/2 a side, 0.275 m at the ratified body. No door in Deli Counter's code needs editing after that: presets.DOOR_W, the width-less default, the staff door and the staff aisle, the stair landing's opening, presets.STAIR_FLIGHT_WIDTH (the corridor plus a cell) and stair_core's punched landing door all read this block. The library's specs carry written widths: run migrate_door_width.py, which widens every authored door under the minimum it reads here, and layout_lint names any that no longer fit. NOT YET FOLLOWING: stairwell.LANDING_DEPTH, the 1.2 m of clear floor at a stair's ends, is a literal. Then rebuild every shell and re-run the gates (the factory's docs/AGENT_CONTRACT.md).
